Sky News live blog — last updated Friday 25 September 2026 17:19 UK. NOTE: THIS IS FRIDAY'S BLOG, NOT TODAY'S. All items below are 25 Sep developments.

HEADLINE: Ukraine war latest: Cars left burning in another deadly strike on Kyiv - as US puts forward new peace talks location

VENUE CLAIM (Friday 25 Sep, 05:55 UK post): The US has proposed a new trilateral meeting with Ukraine and Russia to try to reach a peace deal, Volodymyr Zelenskyy said. New talks could be held in the UAE, with the US suggesting the potential Middle East location.
QUOTE (Zelenskyy, to reporters in a briefing via WhatsApp): "The American side has proposed...a meeting at a technical level in a three-way format." / "We are awaiting a proposal from the United States regarding the date, and the United States has suggested the Emirates as a possible location."

KREMLIN RESPONSE (Friday 25 Sep, 06:20 UK post): The Kremlin has said a trilateral meeting could take place in the near future. The Kremlin, however, said there are no details on a trilateral meeting for the time being.

>>> VERIFICATION STATUS: NO DATE CONFIRMED. Venue is a US SUGGESTION only, reported by Zelenskyy, not a confirmed booking. Kremlin explicitly says no details. Treat as forward-looking and unconfirmed.

EU FUNDS (Friday 25 Sep, 09:30 UK): The EU agreed terms to release EUR 6.6bn (GBP 5.67bn) in funds linked to military aid for Ukraine, EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said.
QUOTE (Kallas): the development was "good news for Ukraine and bad news for Russia". On X: "Moscow's hybrid attacks try to intimidate Europe into scaling back its support for Ukraine. Europe is doing the opposite."
Of the released funds, EUR 900m goes to the EU's military assistance mission for Ukraine, EUR 1bn funds new joint procurement of equipment, and the remaining EUR 4.7bn reimburses member states.

ARCELORMITTAL (Friday 25 Sep, 08:55 UK): Russian strikes have shut Ukraine's biggest steelmaker. ArcelorMittal said it could not restart production at Ukraine's largest steel plant after a series of missile strikes. The Ukrainian government was informed that "safe and sustainable" operations were not possible after four strikes in five weeks caused extensive damage and killed five workers at the south-eastern plant.
QUOTE (Mauro Longobardo, CEO of subsidiary ArcelorMittal Kryvyi Rih): "It is with deep regret that we have concluded that we are no longer able to safely operate ArcelorMittal Kryvyi Rih."

FRIDAY KYIV TOLL: Three killed and seven injured in a daytime drone strike in Kyiv, mayor Vitali Klitschko said. QUOTE (Klitschko, on Telegram): "Cars are burning in the parking lot near the office building where the UAV [unmanned aerial vehicle] hit. Emergency services are working on the scene." Earlier a 14-year-old boy was killed when a Russian drone hit a high-rise building in central Kyiv. (Ukrinform separately reported 7 killed and 59 injured in Kyiv on 25 Sep.)

REFINERIES (Friday): Zelenskyy said Ukraine hit two Russian oil refineries in Perm and Novoshakhtinsk overnight. Rostov Governor Yuri Slyusar said air defences destroyed about 50 drones over the Rostov region and a drone attack damaged the Novoshakhtinsk oil refinery, forcing it to suspend operations temporarily.

BLACK SEA / PORTS ANALYSIS (Sky, Friday, RUSI — approved source):
QUOTE (Dr Sidharth Kaushal, senior research fellow and maritime expert, RUSI, to Sky News): "First, the Russians recognise that denying Ukraine exports and thus hard currency can have a particular impact at this point." / "Secondly, Ukraine's well-known PAC-3 (Patriot interceptor missile) shortfalls have made a strike campaign involving an increasing number of ballistic missiles more appealing for Russia, and striking ports is one part of this campaign."
Dr Kaushal noted Ukraine's government has "very limited fiscal headroom", exacerbated by the failure to reach a legislative bargain which would have secured an IMF loan, and uncertainty over future EU support.
Earlier in the week Russian forces attacked infrastructure in Odesa, including a commercial cargo ship, killing its Ukrainian captain. QUOTE (Ukrainian Sea Ports Authority): "This is yet another Russian terrorist act against civilian shipping. This time, the Russian attack claimed the life of a Ukrainian sailor."

PRIOR TALKS RECORD (Sky explainer): First talks in Belarus/Istanbul 2022, broke down mid-April. May 2025 Istanbul talks lasted barely two hours, no breakthrough but a large-scale prisoner swap. January 2026: first trilateral talks (Russia, Ukraine, US) in Abu Dhabi, UAE — ended with no breakthrough, territory the sticking point. February 2026: Geneva, US-mediated, again no breakthrough.
